claims.text: Transaction-centric methods identify anomalous execution traces but lack awareness of contract semantics, causing legitimate market volatility to be misclassified.

claims.text: Static contract analysis can identify potential vulnerabilities before deployment but ignores runtime behavior and often reports weaknesses that cannot be exploited in practice.
claims.poster_quote: Static contract analysis can identify potential vulnerabilities before deployment but ignores runtime behavior and often reports weaknesses that cannot be exploited in practice.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Conversely, contract-code-based methods focus on uncovering logical vulnerabilities within source code, enabling the proactive identification of potential exploits prior to deployment. ... Conversely, static analyses abstract away runtime behaviors and evolving market conditions, often producing large numbers of theoretical vulnerabilities that cannot be triggered in practice [13].
claims.reason: Section I. The paper states that contract-code-based methods identify exploits prior to deployment but static analyses abstract away runtime behaviors and produce theoretical vulnerabilities that cannot be triggered in practice.

claims.text: DeFiFusion jointly models transaction events and smart contract semantics in a unified Price Manipulation Attack detection pipeline.
claims.poster_quote: DeFiFusion jointly models transaction events and smart contract semantics in a unified Price Manipulation Attack detection pipeline.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We present DeFiFusion, a dual-modal PMA detection framework that closes this gap by jointly modeling transaction events and smart contract semantics within a unified pipeline.
claims.reason: Abstract. The paper states that DeFiFusion jointly models transaction events and smart contract semantics within a unified pipeline.

claims.text: DeFiFusion combines manipulation-aware event encoding, LLM-based contract semantic extraction, and a Dual-Modal Projection-Fusion Transformer with T5-style relative positional encoding.
claims.poster_quote: DeFiFusion combines manipulation-aware event encoding, LLM-based contract semantic extraction, and a Dual-Modal Projection-Fusion Transformer with T5-style relative positional encoding.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Accordingly, we derive price-manipulation-aware event encoding for extracting fine-grained temporal and economic features tailored to manipulation patterns. We further introduce LLM-based contract semantic extraction to supply the execution-logic context that prior behavioral methods lack. To fuse these modalities, we propose a Dual-Modal Projection-Fusion Transformer (DPF-Transformer) with T5-style relative positional encoding...
claims.reason: Abstract. The paper lists these three components as the core of DeFiFusion.

claims.text: The Dual-Modal Projection-Fusion Transformer aligns transaction event vectors with projected contract embeddings.
claims.poster_quote: The Dual-Modal Projection-Fusion Transformer aligns transaction event vectors with projected contract embeddings.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Each ft concatenates the event feature vt ∈ R80 (the row of He) with a learnable projection Wc ct + bc ∈ Rdp of the Phase-2 contract embedding ct (the row of Hc), where dp = 1024.
claims.reason: Section III-D1. The paper describes concatenating the event feature with a projected contract embedding at each position.

claims.text: The shorter modality is zero-padded, and a validity mask ensures that padding contributes to neither attention nor readout.
claims.poster_quote: The shorter modality is zero-padded, and a validity mask ensures that padding contributes to neither attention nor readout.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The two modality sequences are paired index-wise, and the shorter one is zero-padded, so every position carries both modalities. ... A validity mask ρ ∈ {0, 1}L marks authentic positions, so batch padding contributes to neither attention nor readout.
claims.reason: Section III-D1. The paper explicitly states that the shorter modality is zero-padded and a validity mask ensures padding does not contribute to attention or readout.

claims.text: T5-style relative positional encoding introduces a learnable attention bias based on relative event offsets rather than absolute positions.
claims.poster_quote: T5-style relative positional encoding introduces a learnable attention bias based on relative event offsets rather than absolute positions.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: To make attention depend on relative offsets rather than absolute indices, we adopt the T5-RPE, which enters self-attention as a bucketed bias on the logits.
claims.reason: Section III-D1. The paper states that T5-RPE makes attention depend on relative offsets rather than absolute indices via a learnable bias.

claims.text: The encoder contextualizes the fused sequence, followed by masked mean pooling and a bottleneck classification head with dropout.
claims.poster_quote: The encoder contextualizes the fused sequence, followed by masked mean pooling and a bottleneck classification head with dropout.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The encoded sequence Ĥ = (ĥ1 , . . . , ĥL ) is aggregated into one probability by a masked readout and a bottleneck classification head, p̂ = ς(w2 Dp(ReLU(W1 z + b1)) + b2), z = \sum_{t=1}^L \rho_t ĥ_t / \sum_{t=1}^L \rho_t ... The masked mean z weights every authentic event equally and is independent of the padded length. The bottleneck halves the representation, and combined with dropout, keeps the readout capacity small...
claims.reason: Section III-D2. The paper describes the encoder, the masked mean readout (pooling), and the bottleneck classification head with dropout.

claims.text: Global features measure field-filling density and structural payload scale.
